text.p: These are significant stories in the Nigerian press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Large turn-out nationwide on first day in the registration of voters for future elections, a key part of Nigeria's transition to civil rule programme.

- Oil marketing firms, which are now faced with policy of paying cash to state oil firm NNPC for petroleum products they lift, have presented NNPC with their own bill of seven billion naira for transporting fuel to northern parts of Nigeria.
- Some 26 million litres of fuel has been discharged at Apapa port in Lagos while petrol supplies to the city through pipeline have also been boosted following shortages.
- Nigerian supreme court judges can now retire at the age of 70 instead of 65 previously, according to a new decree.
- Inflation rate falls to 26 percent in January from 29 percent in December, says Finance Minister Anthony Ani.
- Central bank mops up 8.5 billion naira from the economy through the sale of treasury bills and treasury bonds.
- Shell restates that it will not resume oil production in the volatile Ogoniland unless it is convinced that the people of the area are willing to accomodate the company.

- A member of a U.N. team due in Nigeria next week says they may be allowed by the authorities to meet detained presidential claimant Moshood Abiola and imprisoned former army ruler Olusegun Obasanjo.
- Nigerian ports authority reviews its procedures to enable delivery of cargo to their owners within 24 hours, says president of ports senior staff association Oddy Enebeli.

- Chief executive of EcoBank Disun Holloway condemns non privatisation of electric authority and telecoms monopoly in 1997 fiscal budget but hails stabilisation of exchange rate, reduced interest rates and fall in inflation.
